paper_title: Morphosyntactic probing of multilingual BERT models
caption: The effect of context masking on case tasks groupby by language family. Error bars indicate the standard deviation.
model_annotation: This bar chart illustrates the effect of context masking on case tasks, grouped by language family, as measured across six different multilingual BERT models: mBERT-L₂ (light blue), XLM-L₂ (dark blue), mBERT-R₂ (light green), XLM-R₂ (dark green), mBERT-B₂ (light red), and XLM-B₂ (dark red). The horizontal axis lists the language families: IE-Baltic, IE-Germanic, IE-Indic, IE-Romance, IE-Slavic family, IE-other, Isolate, Semitic, and Uralic. The vertical axis, labeled "effect," is scaled linearly from 0 to 30, with tick marks at intervals of 10. Each group of bars corresponds to a language family and contains six bars, one for each model, with error bars indicating the standard deviation. The bars are arranged in the order of the legend, with mBERT-L₂ on the left and XLM-B₂ on the right within each group. The heights of the bars vary significantly across families and models; for example, in the IE-Indic family, mBERT-R₂ (light green) shows the highest effect, reaching approximately 21, while XLM-R₂ (dark green) is slightly lower at around 18. In contrast, the Uralic family shows minimal effects, with most bars near 0. The Semitic family exhibits a notable effect for XLM-B₂ (dark red), reaching approximately 19, while mBERT-R₂ (light green) has a negative effect, around -2. The IE-Slavic family shows relatively high effects for mBERT-B₂ (light red, ~17) and XLM-B₂ (dark red, ~16). The IE-Germanic family also shows moderate effects, with mBERT-B₂ (~15) and XLM-B₂ (~14). The Isolate family has uniformly low effects, all near 0. The bars are not sorted by height; instead, they are grouped by language family and ordered according to the model legend. No bars are visually emphasized through shading, bolding, or annotation beyond the standard error bars.
